title: BLF: Adding first support for writing BLF files
description:
Support writing BLF for the following link types:

- Ethernet
- CAN / CAN-FD (socketcan, socketcan over sll)
- FlexRay
- LIN
- Writing Interfaces names in APP_TEXT Channels
- Writing some APP_TEXT Metadata (General, Identity)

Not supported (yet):

- Errors on LIN, CAN, etc.
- BLF internal compression
- EthernetStatus, EthernetPhyStatus

notes.body: It's not exactly my use case (I just need Wireshark to reliably open BLFs, not write them), but this feature can be very useful indeed. I'll take a look at the code to see if I spot anything wrong.

Yes, please do that.

I typically do only need to open BLFs but I had requests that somewhat wanted to look a (filtered) trace but could not open CAN in pcap/pcapng. So I gave it a try.

Here we should probably round up instead of setting it to 0. A payload of 63 bytes would be 64, with one padding byte.
Technically you can't have a CAN-FD payload with a size that's not 0-8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48 or 64. But maybe an abnormal size comes from a truncated payload or some other problem.

CANFD cannot have a payload bigger than 64, so I set it to 0 because it does not make sense. I do not think that truncation is the solution here.

If 64 or less: mapping from length to dlc is done via `canfd_length_to_dlc`

Does this make sense?

However, with the current approach (blf read converts to pcapng linktypes and blf write converts back) we are loosing some metadata! The biggest issue IMHO is the lost interface mapping. BLF uses Interface-IDs per Type and not like pcapng global unique Interface-IDs. And the attached Metdata XMLs may reference to these IDs!

Example BLF interfaces:

* LIN, ID 1
* LIN, ID 2
* Ethernet, ID 1
* CAN, ID 1

We get something like this in pcapng (based on packet order):

* Interface ID 1: "LIN-2"
* Interface ID 2: "Eth-1"
* Interface ID 3: "LIN-1"
* Interface ID 4: "CAN-1"

With the names this is basically ok for today. However, the attached meta data (XML in Upper PDUs) references the orginal IDs. When saving back to BLF, we can currently not construct them.

Written BLF we could this (when we are lucky) or even a completly diff:

* LIN, ID 1 "LIN-2"
* LIN, ID 3 "LIN-1"
* Ethernet, ID 2 "Eth-1"
* CAN, ID 4 "CAN-1"

As the name might be constructed from metadata, we might not have a hint of the original ID in the name.

I am currently considering adding more Metadata to the pcapng (e.g. via Upper PDU) to retain the Interface Mapping. Or maybe we could even "Inject the meta data" even in pcapng!?
Implemented using IDB Interface Descriptions.

Does it preserve the ordering of the interfaces when writing from BLF to BLF? Because Vector software heavily depends on the order of the interfaces.
If CAN2 becomes CAN1, CANoe will not be able to decode messages and signals correctly.

When you open a BLF and just save, it should be identical.

When you open an BLF (with the Meta Data XMLs included) and export (!) back to a BLF, the meta data and the Channel IDs stay the same. However, the format of the frames might change a bit (LIN_Message vs LIN_Message2, etc.).

Also unknown things get removed and Events and Errors too (for now) as the mapping back is not that trivial.

commits_data.message:
BLF: Adding first support for writing BLF files

Support writing BLF for the following link types:
- Ethernet
- CAN / CAN-FD (socketcan, socketcan over sll)
- FlexRay
- LIN
- Writing Interfaces names into APP_TEXT Channels
- Writing some APP_TEXT Metadata (General, Identity)

Not supported (yet):
- Errors on LIN, CAN, etc.
- LIN Events
- BLF internal compression
- EthernetStatus, EthernetPhyStatus
